summary: Cross-examined all 5 target claims. 2 of 5 original claims survive largely intact (parish-partnership scale/QR attribution; church-calendar timing as one lever among several, downgraded from isolated-causal-driver framing). 1 original sub-claim is corrected/strengthened by the counter side (referral LTV lift, now traced to a peer-reviewed study rather than a vendor blog). 3 specific figures/framings fail under scrutiny: the 30% Catholic-collaboration user-increase figure (untraceable), the unqualified calendar-timing-drove-the-spike causal claim (confounded by a rare Ash-Wednesday/Super-Bowl coincidence plus celebrity ad and 15x paid-spend increase), the 83% referral-trust figure (likely misattributed Nielsen WOM stat), and the unqualified 'double-sided rewards are the dominant pattern' framing (real failure modes documented). The authenticity-vs-production claim is genuinely contested: the brief's own best example (Hallow's Super Bowl ad) contradicts its blanket authenticity claim, and no disinterested source resolves it either way -- likely channel-dependent rather than universal. The tactic-transferability-to-FellowScript's-niche question remains correctly unresolved on both sides, as the original brief itself had flagged it as a hypothesis rather than a settled claim. No bounce: counter-evidence was substantive for all 5 claims (not thin), and no claim was found untraceable to its cited source.
